why: The criterion holds for both lines. The FAIL on the first line names a concrete wrong build: bin/csv2json.js always calls `parse(..., '\t')`, or splits on /[\t,]/. It explains why this meets the line, since the TSV printf proof prints the right array. It also explains why the build misses the request: plain CSV without the flag breaks, and commas inside TSV cells get split. The cited files and behaviour are real. bin/csv2json.js, the parse(text, sep) signature in src/parse.js and the 'cli' test in test/csv.test.js all exist. That test would fail if tab splitting were always on, because 'a,b' becomes a single key. The PASS on the README line names the wrong build it tried, a bare '--tsv' mention. It says the line catches it because "documents" needs a usage line, and the real README already uses that usage-example pattern. The overall wrong_build is concrete and consistent with the repository.
